description: Official public-awareness sources for the knowledge corpus. backend/fetch_sources.py downloads the entries marked fetch:true from the publisher into knowledge/documents/ (git-ignored, so each teammate keeps their own copy) and registers them in the local sources.json with approved:false. Nothing here is used for retrieval until a person reviews the file and sets approved:true. Links were checked on 2026-11-16 with HEAD or 1 KB range requests only.

sources.title: WHO — Antimicrobial resistance (fact sheet)
sources.license: Not stated on the page; WHO's copyright policy places WHO publications under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO but does not mention fact sheets.
sources.relevance: Plain-language key facts on AMR and how misuse and overuse drive it.
sources.notes: Saved as extracted text. who.int sometimes needs IPv4; the script prefers IPv4.

sources.title: WHO — Antibiotic resistance: multi-country public awareness survey (2015)
sources.license: Not stated in the IRIS record.
sources.relevance: Common public misconceptions (antibiotics for colds and flu, stopping when better): good material for myth-busting questions.
sources.notes: Direct content link; the /bitstreams/.../download form returns an HTML app shell to scripts. Check whether India is among the surveyed countries before citing it as Indian data.

sources.title: National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (NAP-AMR) 2.0, 2025–2029
sources.publisher: National Centre for Disease Control, MoHFW, Government of India
sources.license: NCDC copyright policy: contents may not be reproduced partially or fully without duly and prominently acknowledging the source.
sources.relevance: India's current national AMR plan; its awareness and community objectives match the project proposal.
sources.notes: Policy document, not a treatment guideline. Large: about 12.9 MB.

sources.title: National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (NAP-AMR) 2017–2021
sources.publisher: National Centre for Disease Control, MoHFW, Government of India
sources.license: NCDC copyright policy: reproduction with due and prominent acknowledgement of the source.
sources.relevance: The original national plan; awareness is strategic priority 1.
sources.notes: Fallback if NAP-AMR 2.0 text extraction fails.

sources.title: NHSRC — Induction Training Module for ASHA (English)
sources.publisher: National Health Systems Resource Centre, National Health Mission
sources.license: NHSRC copyright policy: may be reproduced free of charge without specific permission, accurately, not in a misleading context, with the source acknowledged.
sources.relevance: Written for ASHAs: health, hygiene and illness, infectious diseases, home care and referral for diarrhoea, ARI and fever.
sources.notes: Run the dose scan; leave home-care chapters with medicine amounts out of approval.

sources.title: NHSRC — Notes for ASHA Trainers: Induction Training Module (English)
sources.publisher: National Health Systems Resource Centre, National Health Mission
sources.relevance: Trainer notes; sessions on basic health, hygiene, illness and infectious diseases.

sources.title: NHSRC — Skills That Save Lives: ASHA Module 6 (English)
sources.publisher: National Health Systems Resource Centre, National Health Mission
sources.relevance: Being an ASHA, maternal and newborn health; hygiene and recognising illness for referral.
sources.notes: Off by default: downloaded on 2026-11-16 and found to be scanned images with no extractable text, so it needs OCR before the corpus can use it.

sources.title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices of antibiotic use and AMR in low-income urban Delhi (Antibiotics, 2025)
sources.publisher: MDPI Antibiotics 14(12):1184; Rao S, Basu S, et al. DOI 10.3390/antibiotics14121184
sources.relevance: Community survey: most adults had heard of antibiotics but few knew about AMR; self-medication practices.
sources.notes: Research paper: use for 'common mistakes' questions, citing the finding, not as advice.

sources.title: Primary caregivers' practices and perceptions on antibiotic use and resistance in rural South India (BMJ Open, 2026)
sources.publisher: BMJ Open 16(5):e112630; Charan K, et al. DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2025-112630
sources.relevance: Household antibiotic practices and beliefs of caregivers of children in rural Tamil Nadu, close to the ASHA setting.

sources.title: Social determinants of antibiotic misuse: a qualitative study of community members in Haryana (BMC Public Health, 2017)
sources.publisher: BMC Public Health 17:333; Barker AK, et al. DOI 10.1186/s12889-017-4261-4
sources.relevance: Why villagers obtain antibiotics from pharmacists and informal providers without a prescription.

sources.title: Gamified AMR education for ASHA workers in Mysuru (BMC Medical Education, 2025)
sources.publisher: BMC Medical Education 25:1542; G S VS, Sumana MN, et al. DOI 10.1186/s12909-025-08092-9
sources.license: CC BY-NC-ND (PMC open-access copy); no derivatives, so cite it rather than adapting its text.
sources.relevance: AMR training for ASHAs in Mysuru, Karnataka: directly about this app's users.
sources.notes: Better as evaluation background than as quiz source text, given the no-derivatives licence.

sources.title: NHSRC — Skills That Save Lives: ASHA Module 7, child health and nutrition (English)
sources.publisher: National Health Systems Resource Centre, National Health Mission
sources.relevance: Assessing the sick child, fever, diarrhoea and ARI.
sources.notes: Off by default: its diarrhoea, ARI and fever chapters are likely to give medicine names with amounts, which the README excludes. Fetch with --only only to extract specific reviewed passages.

sources.title: NCDC — AMR posters for the general public (English)
sources.publisher: National Centre for Disease Control, MoHFW
sources.license: NCDC copyright policy: reproduction with due and prominent acknowledgement of the source.
sources.relevance: Official Indian household-facing AMR messages: the closest match to what ASHAs teach.
sources.notes: Off by default: about 109 MB and marked 'Scanned Image', so the corpus cannot read it without OCR. Better to type the poster messages into a reviewed Markdown excerpt.

sources.title: NCDC — Hand hygiene posters (English)
sources.publisher: National Centre for Disease Control, MoHFW
sources.relevance: Handwashing for infection prevention, part of the NCDC AMR campaign.
sources.notes: Off by default: scanned images (OCR needed), about 36 MB.

sources.title: WHO — World Antibiotic Awareness Week 2018 poster: Misuse (Asia scene)
sources.notes: Off by default: a poster with only a few lines of text.
